# How pronounced is populism?

## Absolute and relative frequencies

```{r}
# Overall analysis:
df_gesamt %>%
  count(populismus) %>%
  mutate(Percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Populism distribution overall") %>%
  cols_label(
    populismus = "Populism",
    n = "Count",
    Percent = "Percent (%)"
  )
#### 5% Populistic shares (4256)

# Distribution per broadcast:

# Absolute numbers per broadcast
df_gesamt %>%
  group_by(sendung, populismus) %>%
  summarise(anzahl = n()) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = populismus, values_from = anzahl, values_fill = 0)

# Relative frequencies per broadcast
df_gesamt %>%
  group_by(sendung, populismus) %>%
  summarise(anzahl = n()) %>%
  mutate(anteil = anzahl / sum(anzahl)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = populismus, values_from = c(anzahl, anteil), values_fill = 0)

# Absolute and relative frequencies per broadcast
tab <- df_gesamt %>%
  group_by(sendung, populismus) %>%
  summarise(Anzahl = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(sendung) %>%
  mutate(Percent = round(100 * Anzahl / sum(Anzahl), 1)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

### Table: Populism shares by format

```{r}
gesamt_n   <- nrow(df_gesamt)
gesamt_pop <- sum(df_gesamt$populismus == TRUE)  
# with gridlines
tab %>%
  filter(populismus == TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    sendung = case_when(
      sendung == "Haf" ~ "Hart aber Fair",
      sendung == "Illner" ~ "Maybrit Illner",
      sendung == "Lanz" ~ "Markus Lanz",
      TRUE ~ sendung
    ) ,
    Percent = sprintf("%.1f %%", Percent)  # Percent as string with %
  ) %>%
  select(Broadcast = sendung, Count = Anzahl, Percent) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("Share of populist elements by format")
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c("Count"),
    decimals = 0,
    use_seps = TRUE
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    Broadcast = "Format",
    Count = "Count",
    Percent = "Share of populist elements"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(sides = "all", color = "grey80", weight = px(1)),
    locations = cells_body()
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.border.top.color = "white",
    table.border.bottom.color = "white",
    table.border.top.width = px(0),
    table.border.bottom.width = px(0),
    column_labels.border.top.width = px(0),
    column_labels.border.bottom.width = px(0),
    table.border.left.width = px(0),
    table.border.right.width = px(0),
    heading.background.color = "#f2f2f2",
    table.background.color = "white",
    table.font.size = 14
  ) %>%
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c("Broadcast")
  ) %>%
  cols_align(
    align = "right",
    columns = c("Count", "Percent")
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = md(
      paste0("Total number of sentences: ", gesamt_n, " | Number of populist sentences: ", gesamt_pop)
    )
  )


# without gridlines
```

## Content-related
### Word cloud
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidytext)
library(stopwords)
library(wordcloud2)

# 0. Calculate 95th percentile threshold & filter
schwelle_95 <- quantile(df_gesamt$pop_max, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)
df_pop <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(pop_max > schwelle_95)

# 1. Build extended stopword list
de_stop <- stopwords("de")
filler_words <- c(
  "also","auch","bloß","denn","doch","eben","eigentlich","etwa","halt","ja","mal","nur",
  "schon","vielleicht","wohl","quasi","irgendwie","sozusagen","tja","naja","ne","mein","dein",
  "okay","klar","gut","überhaupt","eventuell","bestimmt","immerhin","sowieso","bisschen","sagen",
  "sogar","natürlich","eher","ziemlich","fast","wirklich","offenbar","meist","meistens","jedenfalls",
  "übrigens","ebenfalls","je","gar","recht","relativ", "dass"
)
custom_stopwords <- c("herr","frau","Herr","Frau")
speaker_tags <- c(paste0("s", 1:99), paste0("s", sprintf("%02d", 1:99)))
all_stopwords <- unique(c(de_stop, filler_words, custom_stopwords, speaker_tags))
all_stopwords_df <- data.frame(word = all_stopwords, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# 2. Remove speaker tags per regex from sentence text
remove_s_speaker_words <- function(text) {
  gsub("\\bs\\d+\\b", "", text, ignore.case = TRUE)
}
df_pop$sentences...20 <- sapply(df_pop$sentences...20, remove_s_speaker_words)

# 3. Tokenize, remove numbers and stopwords, calculate statistics
df_words <- df_pop %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, sentences...20) %>%
  filter(!grepl("^[0-9]+$", word)) %>%              # <--- excludes pure numbers!
  anti_join(all_stopwords_df, by = "word") %>%
  group_by(word) %>%
  summarise(
    freq = n(),
    mean_pop = mean(pop_max, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  filter(freq > 2) # Optional: only words with more than 2 occurrences

# 4. Color scale for word cloud
df_words$score_scaled <- (df_words$mean_pop - min(df_words$mean_pop)) /
                        (max(df_words$mean_pop) - min(df_words$mean_pop))
get_color <- colorRampPalette(c("grey70", "red"))
farben <- get_color(100)
df_words$color <- farben[as.numeric(cut(df_words$score_scaled, breaks = 100))]

# 5. Generate word cloud
wordcloud2(df_words, color = df_words$color)
## large: afd, a,pel, cdu, bevölkerung, bürger
```

## Influence of speakers

## Overview
```{r}
# Calculate share of populist sentences per actor
df_gesamt %>%
  group_by(name, party, job) %>%
  summarise(
    n_gesamt = n(),
    n_pop = sum(populismus == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    anteil_pop = n_pop / n_gesamt,
    beispiel = sentences...20[which(populismus == 1)[1]]
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(anteil_pop)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)
# Weighting difficult

# only participants
df_gesamt %>%
  filter(role == "TN") %>%        # Only participants
  group_by(name, party, job) %>%
  summarise(
    n_gesamt = n(),
    n_pop = sum(populismus == 1, na.rm = TRUE),

    beispiel = sentences...20[which(populismus == 1)[1]]
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(anteil_pop)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)
```

## Role
```{r}
df_gesamt <- df_gesamt %>%
mutate(role = ifelse(role == "R", "E", role)) # Recode R to E (typo in dataset)

populismus_rolle <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(speaker_id != "e_unbekannt_01") %>%
  group_by(role) %>%
  summarise(
    populismus_count = sum(populismus, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_count = n(),
    populismus_share = populismus_count / total_count,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(populismus_rolle, aes(x = role, y = populismus_share, fill = role)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Populism share by role (overall)",
    x = "Role",
    y = "Populism share"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
######### E(6.55%) > TN(5.49%) > Mod (3.67%)
```

### Role per broadcast

```{r}
# per broadcast:
populismus_rolle_sendung <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(speaker_id != "e_unbekannt_01") %>%
  group_by(role, sendung) %>%
  summarise(
    populismus_count = sum(populismus, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_count = n(),
    populismus_share = populismus_count / total_count,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 1. Aggregation: Populism share per role and broadcast, per episode
populismus_box <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(speaker_id != "e_unbekannt_01") %>%
  group_by(role, sendung, show_id) %>%
  summarise(
    populismus_share = sum(populismus, na.rm = TRUE) / n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Boxplot: Distribution by role and broadcast (without time period)
ggplot(populismus_box, aes(x = role, y = populismus_share, fill = sendung)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8), alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Populism share by role and broadcast (boxplot, all time periods)",
    x = "Role",
    y = "Populism share",
    fill = "Broadcast"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

#### Significance test of differences 
```{r}
table_mod <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(role == "Moderation", name %in% c("Maybrit Illner", "Markus Lanz", "Louis Klamroth")) %>%
  mutate(pop = ifelse(populismus == 1, "populistisch", "nicht_populistisch")) %>%
  count(name, pop) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = pop, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

# Build contingency table
mat <- as.matrix(table_mod[,-1])
rownames(mat) <- table_mod$name

# Chi-square test
chisq.test(mat) # highly significant differences

### pairwise comparison
counts <- c(266, 345, 169)         # Populist sentences
totals <- c(5390, 9993, 6025)      # Total sentences
names_vec <- c("Maybrit Illner", "Markus Lanz", "Louis Klamroth")

# Pairwise comparison of populism shares
pairwise.prop.test(
  x = counts,
  n = totals,
  p.adjust.method = "holm",  # Or "bonferroni", "fdr" etc.
  alternative = "two.sided"
) 
# All three moderations differ significantly in the share of populist sentences (p < 0.05 for all comparisons) (Holm)
```

```{r}
 filter(role == "Moderation", name != "Moderator Z") %>%
  group_by(show_id) %>%
  summarise(
    mod_pop_count = sum(populismus, na.rm = TRUE),
    mod_total = n(),
    mod_pop_share = mod_pop_count / mod_total,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Guest list per episode
gaeste_by_episode <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(role == "TN") %>%
  group_by(show_id) %>%
  summarise(gaeste = paste(unique(name), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")

# Combine the two tables
analysis_df <- mod_pop_by_episode %>%
  left_join(gaeste_by_episode, by = "show_id")

# "Long" format: each guest per episode as separate row
guest_long <- analysis_df %>%
  separate_rows(gaeste, sep = "; ") %>%
  rename(guest = gaeste)

# Average moderation populism per guest
gast_pop <- guest_long %>%
  group_by(guest) %>%
  summarise(
    n_auftritte = n(),
    mean_mod_pop_share = mean(mod_pop_share, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_mod_pop_share))

# Visualization: Top 10 guests
gast_pop %>%
  filter(n_auftritte >= 3) %>% # only guests with at least 3 appearances
  top_n(10, mean_mod_pop_share) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(guest, mean_mod_pop_share), y = mean_mod_pop_share)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Average populism share of moderation by guest",
       x = "Guest",
       y = "Populism share moderation (mean)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  theme_minimal()


# Populism share moderation per guest and moderator
gast_pop_moderator <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(role == "Moderation") %>%
  group_by(show_id, moderator = name) %>%
  summarise(
    mod_pop_count = sum(populismus, na.rm = TRUE),
    mod_total = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    df_gesamt %>%
      filter(role == "TN") %>%
      group_by(show_id) %>%
      summarise(gaeste = paste(unique(name), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "show_id"
  ) %>%
  separate_rows(gaeste, sep = "; ") %>%
  rename(guest = gaeste)

# Averages per guest and moderator
vergleich <- gast_pop_moderator %>%
  group_by(moderator, guest) %>%
  summarise(mean_pop_share = mean(mod_pop_count / mod_total, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")



# Comparison table "How populist is moderation on average when guest X sits with Illner – compared to other moderators?"

# 1. Average populism share of moderation per guest (across all shows)
gast_pop_all <- guest_long %>%
  group_by(guest) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_mod_pop_share = mean(mod_pop_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_auftritte = n()
  )

# 2. Shows with Illner as moderator
illner_shows <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(name == "Maybrit Illner", role == "Moderation") %>%
  distinct(show_id)

# 3. Which guests how often at Illner
illner_guests_only <- guest_long %>%
  filter(show_id %in% illner_shows$show_id) %>%
  group_by(guest) %>%
  summarise(n_illner = n())

# 4. Which guests how often with other moderators
andere_guests_only <- guest_long %>%
  filter(!(show_id %in% illner_shows$show_id)) %>%
  group_by(guest) %>%
  summarise(n_andere = n())

# 5. Merge & create comparison table
gast_illner_impact <- gast_pop_all %>%
  left_join(illner_guests_only, by = "guest") %>%
  left_join(andere_guests_only, by = "guest") %>%
  tidyr::replace_na(list(n_illner = 0, n_andere = 0))

# 6. Weighted average of populism shares for guests at Illner and others
mean_pop_illner <- gast_illner_impact %>%
  filter(n_illner > 0) %>%
  summarise(
    gew_pop = weighted.mean(mean_mod_pop_share, n_illner, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>% pull(gew_pop)

mean_pop_andere <- gast_illner_impact %>%
  filter(n_andere > 0) %>%
  summarise(
    gew_pop = weighted.mean(mean_mod_pop_share, n_andere, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>% pull(gew_pop)

# 7. Output of results

cat("Maybrit Illner:", scales::percent(mean_pop_illner, accuracy = 0.1), "\n")
cat("Other moderators:", scales::percent(mean_pop_andere, accuracy = 0.1), "\n")

# 8. Optional: Visualization
```

#### Significance: profession media/culture, politics and business

```{r}
############ Significance 
## ANOVA 
df_satz <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(role == "TN", job %in% c("Politik", "Medien und Kultur", "Wirtschaft"))

for (s in unique(df_satz$sendung)) {
  cat("\n---", s, "---\n")
  print(summary(aov(populismus ~ job, data = filter(df_satz, sendung == s))))
}
### In all three cases, p-value << 0.05 (e.g., 0.00083, 1.58e-09, 4.5e-09): There are significant differences in populism share between professional groups in all three broadcasts
# The professional group (job) explains a significant proportion of the variance in populism (populismus) within each broadcast.


# Which groups
for (s in unique(df_satz$sendung)) {
  cat("\n---", s, "TukeyHSD ---\n")
  model <- aov(populismus ~ job, data = filter(df_satz, sendung == s))
  print(TukeyHSD(model))
}
# Media and culture usually has the highest populism share (except in HaF, where there's no difference to politics). Business is least populist in HaF; in the other broadcasts there are no significant differences to politics. Politics is significantly less populist than "media and culture" in "Illner" and "Lanz".

### Content-related
# Why does "media and culture" often show higher populism shares? (e.g., media staging, role understanding)
# Why is "business" so much less populist in one broadcast? (e.g., expert status, neutrality obligation)
# Politics: Diplomacy, stability -> parties question whether government or not
```

#### Content-related: Heatmap

```{r}
professions <- unique(df_gesamt$job)

# Stopwords
df_pop <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(pop_max > schwelle_95)

# 1. Build extended stopword list
de_stop <- stopwords("de")
filler_words <- c(
  "also","auch","bloß","denn","doch","eben","eigentlich","etwa","halt","ja","mal","nur",
  "schon","vielleicht","wohl","quasi","irgendwie","sozusagen","tja","naja","ne","mein","dein",
  "okay","klar","gut","überhaupt","eventuell","bestimmt","immerhin","sowieso","bisschen","sagen",
  "sogar","natürlich","eher","ziemlich","fast","wirklich","offenbar","meist","meistens","jedenfalls",
  "übrigens","ebenfalls","je","gar","recht","relativ", "dass"
)
custom_stopwords <- c("herr","frau","Herr","Frau")
speaker_tags <- c(paste0("s", 1:99), paste0("s", sprintf("%02d", 1:99)))
all_stopwords <- unique(c(de_stop, filler_words, custom_stopwords, speaker_tags))
all_stopwords_df <- data.frame(word = all_stopwords, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# 2. Remove speaker tags per regex from sentence text
remove_s_speaker_words <- function(text) {
  gsub("\\bs\\d+\\b", "", text, ignore.case = TRUE)
}
df_pop$sentences...20 <- sapply(df_pop$sentences...20, remove_s_speaker_words)

# 3. Tokenize, remove numbers and stopwords, calculate statistics
df_words <- df_pop %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, sentences...20) %>%
  filter(!grepl("^[0-9]+$", word)) %>%              # <--- excludes pure numbers!
  anti_join(all_stopwords_df, by = "word") %>%
  group_by(word) %>%
  summarise(
    freq = n(),
    mean_pop = mean(pop_max, na.rm = TRUE))

# Empty list for results
top_words_per_job <- list()

for (profession in professions) {
  df_sub <- df_pop %>%
    filter(job == profession, populismus == TRUE)
  
  words <- df_sub %>%
    unnest_tokens(word, sentences...20) %>%
    anti_join(all_stopwords_df, by = "word") %>%
    filter(!grepl("^[0-9]+$", word)) %>%  # Removes pure numbers
    count(word, sort = TRUE)
  
  # Save top 10
  top_words_per_job[[profession]] <- head(words, 10)
}

# Top-10 words for all professions as dataframe
top_words_all <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(top_words_per_job), function(job) {
    d <- top_words_per_job[[job]]
    d$job <- job
    d
  })
)

# Optional: consider only top 20 words overall
top_gesamt <- top_words_all %>%
  group_by(word) %>%
  summarise(gesamt = sum(n)) %>%
  arrange(desc(gesamt)) %>%
  slice(1:20)

top_words_filtered <- top_words_all %>%
  filter(word %in% top_gesamt$word) %>%
  left_join(top_gesamt, by = "word")

top_words_filtered <- top_words_filtered %>%
  filter(job != "unbekannt")


# Additional info
## Calculate additional info
n_professions <- length(unique(top_words_filtered$job))
n_words <- length(unique(top_words_filtered$word))
professions_list <- paste(unique(top_words_filtered$job), collapse = ", ")

## How many sentences were evaluated per profession?
sentence_count <- df_pop %>%
  filter(populismus == TRUE, job %in% unique(top_words_filtered$job)) %>%
  group_by(job) %>%
  summarise(Sentences = n())

# Version 1
ggplot(top_words_filtered, aes(x = job, y = reorder(word, gesamt), fill = n)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(x = "Profession", y = "Word", fill = "Frequency", title = "Top populism terms by profession") +
  theme_minimal()


# Version 2
ggplot(top_words_filtered, aes(x = job, y = reorder(word, gesamt), fill = n)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "Top populism terms by profession",
    subtitle = paste0(
      n_words, " most frequent words (populist sentences), ",
      n_professions, " profession groups: ", professions_list
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Filter: German-language and extended stopwords, pure numbers removed.\n",
      "Basis: populist sentences from talk shows, top-10 words per profession, consolidated to 20 most frequent overall.",
      "\nNumber of evaluated populist sentences per profession:\n",
      paste(sentence_count$job, sentence_count$Sentences, sep=": ", collapse=" | ")
    ),
    x = "Profession",
    y = "Word",
    fill = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

job_labels <- c(
  "Expert",
  "Media\nand Culture",
  "Public",
  "Politics",
  "Business",
  "Science"
)


heatmap_job <- ggplot(top_words_filtered, aes(x = job, y = reorder(word, gesamt), fill = n)) +

    subtitle = "Distribution of 20 most-mentioned words in populist statements",
    x = "Profession of guests",       
    y = "Word"
  ) +
      scale_x_discrete(labels = job_labels) + 
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 17, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(t = 25)),
    panel.grid = element_blank(), 
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box.margin = margin(0, 40, 0, 0),
    legend.title.align = 0.5,
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 25)),

  ) +

  ))
```

### Scatterplot: Individuals in parties per broadcast
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)

# Share of populist sentences per person and broadcast
df_politicians <- df_gesamt %>%
  filter(
    role == "TN",
    job == "Politik",
    !party %in% c("Ausland", "NA"),
    !is.na(party)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    party = case_when(
      party %in% c("CDU", "CSU") ~ "Union",
      TRUE ~ party
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(name, party, sendung) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sentences = n(),                                  # Total sentences/utterances
    n_pop_sentences = sum(populismus == 1, na.rm = TRUE), # Populist sentences
    pop_sentence_share = n_pop_sentences / n_sentences,    # Share of populist sentences
    mean_Anti_Elitism = mean(Anti_Elitism, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_People_Centrism = mean(People_Centrism, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    lastname = stringr::word(name, -1)
  )

# Top 10 politicians per party & broadcast by populism share
df_top5 <- df_politicians %>%
  group_by(party, sendung) %>%
  arrange(desc(pop_sentence_share)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  ungroup()

# Version 1: Populism share as transparency/size/color possible!
ggplot(df_politicians, aes(
  x = mean_Anti_Elitism,
  y = mean_People_Centrism,
  color = party,
  size = n,
  alpha = pop_sentence_share
)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(
    data = df_top5,
    aes(label = lastname),
    hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.01,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 8)) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.3, 1), name = "Populism share (sentences)") +
  facet_grid(party ~ sendung) +
  scale_color_manual(values = parteifarben) +
  labs(
    x = "Anti-Elitism",
    y = "People-Centrism",
    color = "Party",
    size = "Mentions",
    alpha = "Populism share (sentences)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    strip.text.y = element_blank()
  )

### Take-aways
### Wagenknecht at HaF much higher anti-elite
# Populism is overall rare (in talk shows, among most politicians).
# Individual politicians (esp. from AfD, BSW, Left) show significantly higher populism shares.
# Distribution varies depending on broadcast and party.
# The majority of established parties (SPD, CDU/CSU, Greens, FDP) express themselves very rarely in populist ways in talk shows.
# BSW: Wagenknecht is the central, outstanding point: She has comparatively high populism share across all shows (larger point size). She also ranks very high on both anti-elitism and people-centrism, meaning she expresses particularly populist rhetoric and uses corresponding rhetorical elements. Other BSW representatives (e.g., Ali, Lafontaine, Masi) sometimes have lower populism shares and vary in their values – but the overall spread remains high.
# The strong spread of populist elements among the Left is due to the heterogeneity of the other left-wing politicians. The large spread in BSW is mainly caused by Wagenknecht herself and possibly one or two other actors in your dataset.
# Left and BSW: Different party factions and individual profiles lead to a wide range of populist rhetoric.
```

# Temporal progression

## Time period definition
```{r}
# Which time periods are considered?
# Rest April 2024 - November 2024 (01.04.24 - 05.11.24)
# VF: November 24 - Dec 25 (06.11.24 - 31.12.24)
# BTW: January 25 - Feb 25 (01.01.25 - 23.02.25)

df_gesamt <- df_gesamt %>%
  mutate(
    zeitraum = case_when(
      date >= as.Date("2024-04-01") & date <= as.Date("2024-11-05") ~ "Rest",
      date >= as.Date("2024-11-06") & date <= as.Date("2024-12-31") ~ "Confidence vote",
      date >= as.Date("2025-01-01") & date <= as.Date("2025-02-23") ~ "Federal election",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```


## Overview
```{r}
# Join time period (if not already included)
populismus_zeit <- df_gesamt %>%
  group_by(date, zeitraum) %>%
  summarise(
    populismus_count = sum(populismus, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_count = n(),
    populismus_share = populismus_count / total_count,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(populismus_zeit, aes(x = date, y = populismus_share, color = zeitraum)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Populism share over time by time period",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Populism share"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

### Peak shortly before federal election, low during confidence vote, rest relatively constant
```

```{r}
# Calculation: share per broadcast and time period

# Step 1: Calculate share per broadcast (episode) and time period
pro_episode <- df_gesamt %>%
  group_by(sendung, zeitraum, show_id, date) %>%
  summarise(
    populismus_count = sum(populismus, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_count = n(),
    populismus_share = populismus_count / total_count,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pro_episode$zeitraum <- factor(
  pro_episode$zeitraum,
  levels = c("Rest", "Confidence vote", "Federal election")
)

# Boxplot with N integrated:

# Table with N per show and time period
n_table <- pro_episode %>%
  group_by(sendung, zeitraum) %>%
  summarise(N = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = zeitraum, values_from = N, values_fill = 0)

# Build text for caption
n_legend <- paste(
  apply(n_table, 1, function(row) {
    sprintf("%s: Rest=%s, Confidence vote=%s, Federal election=%s",
            row["sendung"], row["Rest"], row["Confidence vote"], row["Federal election"])
  }),
  collapse = "\n"
)

# Version 1
ggplot(pro_episode, aes(x = zeitraum, y = populismus_share, fill = sendung)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2, dodge.width = 0.8), alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sendungsfarben, name = "Broadcast") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +  # <-- HERE!
  labs(
    x = "Time period",
    y = "Share of populist statements per broadcast (%)",
    title = "Populism share per individual broadcast by time period and format",
    fill = "Broadcast",
    caption = paste("N per format and time period:\n", n_legend)
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Raincloud: Formats over time
```{r}
  # Generate n labels per group
labels_n <- labels %>%
  arrange(zeitraum, sendung) %>%
  mutate(txt = paste0(sendung, " (", zeitraum, "): n = ", n))
n_text <- labels %>%
  arrange(zeitraum, sendung) %>%
  mutate(txt = paste0(sendung, ": n = ", n)) %>%
  group_by(zeitraum) %>%
  summarise(txt = paste(txt, collapse = "; ")) %>%
  mutate(txt = paste0(zeitraum, ":\n", txt)) %>%
  pull(txt) %>%
  paste(collapse = "\n\n") # Paragraph after each time period

dodge_width <- 0.8  # or another value depending on desired spacing

# Then in the plot:
raincloud_zeit_proformat <- ggplot(pro_episode, aes(x = zeitraum, y = populismus_share, fill = sendung, color = sendung)) +
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(
    adjust = .5, width = .3, justification = -.18, .width = 0,
    point_colour = NA, position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width), alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = .13, outlier.color = NA, fill = NA, color = "black",
    position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width)
  ) +
  ggdist::stat_dots(
    side = "left", justification = 1.08, binwidth = .01, dotsize = 0.08,
    position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width), alpha = 0.3, color = "grey30"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sendungsfarben, name = "Format") +
  scale_color_manual(values = sendungsfarben, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, 0.12), breaks = seq(0, 0.12, 0.02),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time period",
    y = "Share of populist statements per format (%)",
    title = "Raincloud plot: Populism share per individual broadcast by time period and format",
    fill = "Broadcast format",
    caption = paste0("Point: mean per group, n = number of broadcasts\n", n_text)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
ggsave("raincloud_zeit_proformat.png", raincloud_zeit_proformat, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

## Significance tests: Time periods

```{r}
# For the time period "Rest"
rest_data <- pro_episode %>% filter(zeitraum == "Rest")
kruskal.test(populismus_share ~ sendung, data = rest_data)
# Post-hoc test:
pairwise.wilcox.test(rest_data$populismus_share, rest_data$sendung)
########### In the time period "Rest", broadcasts do not differ significantly in populism share. The distribution of populism share is therefore similar across "HaF", "Illner" and "Lanz" in this period.

# For the time period "Confidence vote"
vf_data <- pro_episode %>% filter(zeitraum == "Confidence vote")
kruskal.test(populismus_share ~ sendung, data = vf_data)
# Post-hoc test:
pairwise.wilcox.test(vf_data$populismus_share, vf_data$sendung)
######### In the time period "Confidence vote", talk shows (HaF, Illner, Lanz) show no statistically significant differences in the share of populist statements per broadcast. The results confirm that the populism share in this period is comparable between broadcasts.

# For the time period "Federal election"
btw_data <- pro_episode %>% filter(zeitraum == "Federal election")
kruskal.test(populismus_share ~ sendung, data=btw_data)
# Post-hoc test:
pairwise.wilcox.test(btw_data$populismus_share, btw_data$sendung)
##########  no significant difference in the share of populist statements per broadcast. Both the overall test and pairwise comparisons show that broadcasts do not differ statistically from each other in this period in terms of populism share.

############# overall also no significant differences
```

```{r}
    title = "Temporal progression: Populism share by profession and broadcast",
    x = "Time period",
    y = "Share of populist statements",
    color = "Profession"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


## CONCLUSION:
# Media and culture is the profession group with the highest populism share in every time period. Particularly high during federal election. (Federal election: 9.2% Confidence vote: 7.5% Rest: 6.1%)
# Politics also shows a decline in populism share from "Federal election" to "Confidence vote". The share is always below "Media and culture". (Federal election: 6.3% Confidence vote: 4.6% Rest: 5.4%)
# Business moves between politics and media/culture, with a slight increase during "Confidence vote". (Federal election: 6.1% Confidence vote: 5.2% Rest: 4.3%)
# Science remains consistently low and shows no major differences between time periods. (Federal election: 5.7% Confidence vote: 3.7% Rest: 3.7%)
# Expert: Share drops in "Confidence vote" to 1.4% (otherwise 4.3–5.3%)
# Public: Share also particularly low during "Confidence vote" (1.4%), otherwise 3.3–5.1%

# The profession group differences are much more pronounced than temporal fluctuations.

```

```{r}
# Populism share per party and time period
```

```{r}
### Illner really only invited greens, SPD and union during confidence vote


# Populism share is party-dependent: AfD and BSW clearly stand out.
# Broadcast effect: "Hart aber fair" more often provides an environment where populist statements are made – especially for AfD, BSW and Left.
# Temporal consistency: Party and broadcast-specific differences are more stable than differences between time periods.

## Comparison of time periods
# The graphic shows for each party and each broadcast the populism share in three time periods ("Rest", "Confidence vote", "Federal election"), each in separate panels.
# Basic patterns (e.g., AfD and BSW highest, Greens/FDP/SPD/Union lower) repeat across all three time periods.
# Bar heights fluctuate from period to period, but the relationship between parties remains constant.
```

```{r}
# 1. Share of populist sentences per person, broadcast and time period (new name!)
```
